record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.context_brief: Invariant subspaces of the Bergman shift
record.original_question: Let D be the open unit disk in the complex plane, let dS be normalized area measure on D, and let L^2_a(D) be the Bergman space of analytic functions on D with finite integral of |f|^2 against dS. A closed subspace J of L^2_a(D) is z-invariant when zf belongs to J for every f in J. Characterize all z-invariant closed subspaces of L^2_a(D).

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 1 Characterize the invariant subspaces of L2a(D).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disk in the complex plane, and let $dS$ denote normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$ (so $\int_{\mathbb{D}} dS = 1$). The Bergman space $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is the Hilbert space of analytic functions $f : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that
$$\|f\|^2 = \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2 \, dS(z) < \infty,$$
endowed with the inner product $\langle f, g \rangle = \int_{\mathbb{D}} f(z)\overline{g(z)}\, dS(z)$. A closed subspace $J \subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called $z$-invariant (invariant under the Bergman shift) if $zf \in J$ for every $f \in J$.

Provide a complete characterization (description / classification) of all $z$-invariant closed subspaces $J$ of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$, analogous to Beurling's theorem for the Hardy space $H^2$ of the disk.
artifact.status_search_result: A full characterization of the invariant subspaces of the Bergman space $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ remains a well-known open problem. Substantial partial progress is known (Aleman–Richter–Sundberg's theorem that $J = [J \ominus zJ]$, the existence of multipliers with arbitrarily large index, Hedenmalm's theory of contractive zero-divisors, etc.), but no Beurling-type classification has been obtained. Recent surveys and works through 2024 continue to list it as open.

status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to study partial structural results rather than a full classification.
